title: Give each signal a defensible next step.
intro: A proposed workflow for Profound’s pre-sales team: separate buying intent from noise, resolve account identity and route a useful brief to a rep who can act.
notice: All accounts, events, scores and outcomes are synthetic. This is an internal GTM workflow proposal, not Profound product data or measured company performance.

records.name: Cobalt Travel
records.context: Marketing operations wants to connect AI-search reporting with campaign planning.
records.question: Which AI-search questions would change your next campaign decision?

records.name: Cedar Retail
records.context: A team is comparing AI visibility tools; evaluation ownership is not established.
records.question: Who owns the evaluation and what would a useful first result look like?

records.name: Tern Software
records.context: Heavy content activity with no stated evaluation or buying timeframe.
records.question: Is this research for an active project or general learning?

records.name: Moss Home
records.context: An agency submitted a form on behalf of an unverified brand.
records.source: Synthetic form with an unresolved brand relationship
records.question: Which legal account and brand should own this evaluation?

records.name: Lumen Tools
records.context: An old request resurfaced during a backfill.
records.question: Is the project still active, and is the original request current?

records.name: Birch Finance
records.context: An existing opportunity received fresh evaluation activity.
records.source: Synthetic pricing event joined to an open opportunity
records.question: What changed since the account owner’s last conversation?

records.name: Sable Commerce
records.context: A later reply requested no further prospecting contact.
records.question: Preserve the request and let an existing owner review any relationship.

records.name: Pine Media
records.context: An event conversation raised questions about citations and content planning.
records.question: Which team would act on an AI-search visibility gap?

experiments.name: Intent over volume
experiments.hypothesis: Explicit evaluation signals produce more useful rep conversations than a page-view threshold.
experiments.treatment: Prioritize reviewed intent and current account context
experiments.guardrail: Missed high-intent accounts and review time
experiments.allocation: Randomize eligible accounts within segment and region

experiments.name: Evidence in the rep brief
experiments.hypothesis: A source and discovery question reduce time spent reconstructing context.
experiments.treatment: Intent reason, source, owner and discovery question
experiments.primary: Accepted rep handoffs within one business day
experiments.allocation: Compare matched rep queues with a fixed observation window

roadmap.title: Trace the entry paths
roadmap.body: Map forms, events and outbound responses with sales. Agree on identity keys, intent definitions and an exception queue. Ship one reviewed rep brief.
roadmap.measure: Source accuracy, missing identities and rep acceptance

roadmap.title: Make routing dependable
roadmap.body: Add territory, company-size and capacity rules. Preserve existing ownership, make retries safe and keep rejected handoffs visible.
roadmap.measure: Misroutes, duplicate assignments and time to acceptance

roadmap.title: Test pipeline quality
roadmap.body: Compare intent rules against the existing process using account-level cohorts. Separate held meetings and qualified opportunities from activity volume.
roadmap.measure: Qualified pipeline, rep usage and enrichment cost per useful brief

aiApplication: At Profound, I would use bounded research agents to attach evidence to each account signal, then validate the recommendation before a seller acts. My MCP analytics experience would support a loop that measures qualified outcomes and learns from rejected signals.
